title: Thirty pieces of silver — the price of the shepherd, cast to the potter in the house of Yahuah (the LORD) (Zechariah 11; Exodus 21; Psalm 41)
summary:
It ain't new. Judas sets a price and the priests agree to it:

*And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.* (Matthew 26:15)

Zechariah had already been paid that sum for shepherding the flock, and had already thrown it where Judas would throw it:

*And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver.* (Zechariah 11:12)

*And Yahuah (LORD) said unto me, Cast it unto the potter: a goodly price that I was prised at of them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them to the potter in the house of Yahuah (LORD).* (Zechariah 11:13)

*A goodly price that I was prised at of them*: thirty pieces was the sum the Torah set for a slave killed by an ox, the worth of a servant's life and no more:

*If the ox shall push a manservant or a maidservant; he shall give unto their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.* (Exodus 21:32)

The shepherd of the house was valued at a gored servant, and Matthew closes the account where Zechariah left it, with the silver thrown back in the temple and spent on a potter's field:

*Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued, whom they of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) did value;* (Matthew 27:9)

*And gave them for the potter’s field, as Yahuah (Lord) appointed me.* (Matthew 27:10)

The betrayer himself was written too, by David, and Yahusha (Jesus) said so at the table with Judas still in the room:

*Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.* (Psalm 41:9)

*I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me.* (John 13:18)

The price, the potter, the house of Yahuah (the LORD), the friend who ate his bread: none of it took him by surprise. He walked into what the prophets had written and let Judas play his part in it.

3087.prose: The man who went to the chief priests to bargain goes back to the same men with the money in his hand. The silver returns to the ones who weighed it out. Then it is cast down in the temple, as Zechariah threw his thirty into the house of Yahuah (LORD).
3087.phrase: brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders
3087.sentence: Judas carries the thirty pieces back to the same chief priests he first went to, and casts them down in the temple.

3088.prose: Judas has gone to the priests, and the next verse sets the sum. It was already weighed out to the shepherd. Zechariah the prophet asked for his wages with *give me my price*, and they counted him out thirty pieces of silver.
3088.phrase: So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver
3088.sentence: The shepherd's price of thirty pieces of silver is the same sum the priests will count out for Judas's bargain.

3089.prose: Thirty is not a random sum. The Torah sets it as the price of a servant killed by an ox. The priests set on Yahusha (Jesus) the worth of a gored servant's life, and no more.
3089.phrase: he shall give unto their master thirty shekels of silver
3089.sentence: The Torah's price for a servant killed by an ox is the thirty the priests agree to pay.

3090.prose: Judas is one of the twelve, a man who sat at the table. David wrote of a friend who *did eat of my bread* and turned on him. The man going to the priests is that friend, and he was in the writings before he was at the table.
3090.phrase: in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me
3090.sentence: David's trusted friend who ate his bread and turned on him is the betrayer Judas becomes.

3091.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says it with Judas still in the room. He knows whom he chose, and he gives David's line about the friend who eats his bread and lifts his heel. The man who goes to the priests does not catch him off guard.
3091.phrase: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled
3091.sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) names the betrayal as written, and says he knew who he chose.

3092.prose: Long before Judas went to the priests, Yahusha (Jesus) told the twelve that one of them was a devil. The next verse names Judas. The betrayal was seen from far back on the road, the same as the prophets had it.
3092.phrase: Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?
3092.sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) names the traitor among the twelve long before the silver is counted.

3093.prose: Peter reads the whole matter back to the hundred and twenty. David spoke it beforehand about Judas, who led the men to Yahusha (Jesus). What Judas did on his way to the priests had already come out of the mouth of David.
3093.phrase: this scripture must needs have been fulfilled, which the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by the mouth of David spake before concerning Judas
3093.sentence: Peter says David spoke beforehand about Judas, so the betrayal was written ahead.

3094.prose: The proverb sorts friends from enemies. Judas is called one of the twelve, a friend at the table, yet he goes to the priests to deal. Proverbs says what that is, however friendly the hand: an enemy's kiss is deceitful.
3094.phrase: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful
3094.sentence: A friend's wounds can be trusted, but a false friend's show of love hides the betrayal.

5305.prose: Judas goes to hand Yahusha (Jesus) over, and the money the priests promise next has a history. Zechariah had already been weighed out thirty pieces of silver as his price for shepherding. The price Judas takes is the shepherd's price.
5305.phrase: So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver
5305.sentence: The thirty pieces weighed to the shepherd are the price Judas takes for Yahusha (Jesus).

5306.prose: Matthew tells the same moment and the same man, walking to the chief priests. Mark says he came to betray. Matthew's next lines add what he asked and what they gave, thirty pieces of silver, and that sum is Zechariah's.
5306.phrase: one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests
5306.sentence: Matthew gives the same going to the priests and goes on to the bargain for silver.

5307.prose: Mark shows Judas going. John shows what was in his heart before he went. Yahusha (Jesus) knew his hour was come, and was not taken by surprise by the man who carried out the bargain.
5307.phrase: the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him
5307.sentence: John shows what was in Judas's heart at supper before he went to the priests.
